newsitem.title: MOROCCO: FOCUS-Moroccan airline draws 1997-2001 strategy plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Moroccan airline draws 1997-2001 strategy plan.

text.p: Morocco's airline Royal Air Maroc (RAM), on Wednesday outlined a 1997-2001 strategy plan aims to modernise its fleet, reduce the debt ratio, and reach a $600 million annual turnover target.

In a detailed report sent to Reuters on Wednesday, Royal Air Maroc said: "It launched a five-year strategic plan which targets the activity growth, deep modernisation of its fleet and infrastructure and setting up a strong strategic alliances."

Despite the tariffs drop by an average five percent and a rise of aircrafts' fuel price by 25 percent in 1996, the firm reached "good results in 1996 thanks to the downsizing costs policy," the report said.

The airline, which forecast a 270 million dirhams ($28.4 million) net profit by end 1997, up from up from 145 million dirhams last year, said it was "committed to continue its downsizing costs policy and reducing the debt ratio to meet the international standard."
The debt ratio (debt/shareholders equity) which stands at 3.1 in 1996, is expected to drop to 2.44 and reach the target of 1.9 by the year 2001, a company manager said.

The manager said: "the firm was in the red with 46.9 million dirhams loss in 1994 before management change...The results has dramatically improved since with net profits of 91.6 million dirhams in 1995 and 145 million in 1996".
The airline chairman Mohamed Hassad earlier said "the debt weight represented 7.5 percent of the turnover in 1995/96 and we plan to reduce it to 6.0 percent by the year 2000/01."

The company's 1996 results showed a turnover of 4.7 billion dirhams, up 1.5 percent in 1995. It plans to reach more than 6.0 billion dirhams ($638 million) by the end of the strategic plan five-year period.
"Our prime target is to go beyond the 6.0 billion dirhams turnover by the year 2001 in order to realise an annual net profit of 5.0 percent of annual total turnover," Hassad said.
The company decided to invest 4.5 billion dirhams on a five-year period, of which 3.8 billion will be devoted to purchase moderne aircrafts, including Boeing 732 planes, the report said.

"The objective is to replace the older planes Boeing 737-200 by two new aircrafts every year to reduce the average age of the fleet to five years from the current 11 years," the report added. RAM has at present six medium and short distance Boeing 737-200 planes.

Royal Air Maroc also plans to double it capital to 2.0 billion dirhams from the current 1.0 billion dirhams as part of the modernisation programme and introduction of a stake of its stock on the Casablanca bourse in future.
"My plan is to float up to 30 percent of the firm's capital on the Casablanca bourse by end 1998, which aims at more transparency and improve the national airline image," Hassad said.
If the floatation plan is accepted by the government, "the company will go ahead with the project to increase investments and improve its competitiveness," he said.

In a move to reinforce its position in France, Royal Air Maroc signed an agreement of partnership with French Air France last week. "It will also enable the Moroccan airline to get access to more than 200 cities in North America through Air France network," an official said.

The government has a majority stake of 94 percent while French Air France holds 3.9 percent and Spanish Iberia has 1.3 percent and the remaining stake is held by other private investors, including the conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement.
RAM which serves 64 cities in Europe, Africa, the Middle East and United States, carried more than 2.4 million passengers in 1996, up 7.2 percent compared with the previous year, the report added.
